cues.en: Hi. So sometimes people ask how I can predict what an artificial general intelligence might do. They say something like, you seem to be predicting that AIs would take these quite specific actions, trying to prevent themselves from being turned off, preventing themselves from being modified, improving themselves, acquiring resources. Why do you think that an AGI would have these specific goals? Surely we haven't built the thing yet. We don't know anything about it. It might want anything.
cues.zh: 嗨。有时候大家会问，我怎么能预测通用人工智能会做什么。他们会说，你似乎在预测 AI 会采取某些非常具体的行动，比如防止自己被关机、防止自己被修改、进行自我提升、获取资源。你凭什么认为 AGI 会有这些具体的目标呢？毕竟我们现在还没把它造出来。我们对它一无所知。它可能想要任何东西。

cues.en: Aren't you making a lot of unwarranted assumptions? Well, the reason that I make these predictions is because of something called instrumental convergence, which actually relies on surprisingly few assumptions. The main assumption I'm making is that an AGI will behave like an agent. An agent is basically just a thing that has goals or preferences, and it takes actions to achieve those goals or to satisfy those preferences. So the simplest thing that you might think of as an agent is something like a thermostat.
cues.zh: 你这不是做了很多毫无根据的假设吗？其实，我做出这些预测的原因，是一种叫做“工具性收敛”的现象，而它所依赖的假设其实少得惊人。我所做的核心假设就是，AGI 的行为会像一个智能体。智能体本质上就是一种拥有目标或偏好的实体，并且会采取行动来实现这些目标或满足这些偏好。你可以想象到的最简单的智能体，大概就是温控器之类的东西了。

cues.en: It has a goal, which is for the room to be at a particular temperature, and it has actions it can take in the form of turning on the heating or turning on the air conditioning. And it takes actions to achieve its goal of keeping the room at a particular temperature. That's like an extremely simple agent. A slightly more complex agent might be something like a chess AI. Its goal is to win the chess game, to have the opponent's king in checkmate. It can take actions in the form of moving its pieces on the board, and it chooses its actions in order to achieve the goal of winning the game.
cues.zh: 它的目标是让房间保持在特定温度，它可以采取的行动就是打开暖气或打开空调。它通过采取行动来达成将房间维持在特定温度的目标。这就是一个极其简单的智能体。稍微复杂一点的智能体可能就像国际象棋 AI。它的目标是赢得棋局，将死对手的国王。它可以采取的行动是在棋盘上移动棋子，它选择这些行动来达成赢得比赛的目标。

cues.en: The idea of an agent is popular in economics, where it's common to model companies and individual human beings as rational agents. For the sake of simplicity, it's often assumed that the goal of human beings is to acquire money, that their utility is just proportional to how much money they have. This is obviously a huge oversimplification, and it's a very popular fact that most people are motivated by a lot of things, not just money. But while it's easy to point out the shortcomings that this assumption has, what's remarkable to me is how well it works.
cues.zh: 智能体的概念在经济学中很常见，人们通常会将公司和个人建模为理性智能体。为了简便起见，通常会假设人类的目标就是赚钱，其效用与拥有的金钱数量成正比。这显然是一个极大的过度简化，众所周知，大多数人的动机来自于很多事情，而不仅仅是金钱。但是，尽管指出这种假设的缺陷很容易，真正让我感到惊讶的是它的效果居然这么好。

cues.en: or that it even works at all. It's true that most people use a very complex utility function, which looks nothing like the basic goal of get as much money as you can. But surprisingly, even very simple economic models that rely on this simplifying assumption can provide some really useful and powerful tools for thinking about the behaviour of people, companies and societies. Why is that?
cues.zh: 甚至怀疑它到底起不起作用。确实，大多数人所使用的效用函数非常复杂，根本不像“赚尽可能多的钱”这种基本目标那么简单。但令人惊讶的是，即使是依赖这种简化假设的极其简单的经济模型，也能为思考个人、公司和社会的行为提供一些非常实用且强大的工具。这是为什么呢？

cues.en: I think it has to do with the nature of terminal goals and instrumental goals. I talked about this in a lot more detail in the orthogonality thesis video, which I would recommend checking out if you haven't seen it yet. But to give a quick summary, your terminal goals are the things that you want just because you want them. You don't have a reason to want them particularly, they're just what you want. Whereas instrumental goals are goals that you want as a way of getting some other goal.
cues.zh: 我认为这与终极目标和工具性目标的本质有关。我在关于正交性假说的视频中更详细地讨论过这一点，如果你还没看过，建议去看一下。不过简单概括一下，终极目标就是那些你单纯因为想得到而想要的东西。你没有特别的理由去追求它们，它们本身就是你的渴望。而工具性目标则是你为了实现其他目标而追求的目标。

cues.en: So, for example, in chess, you want to take your opponent's queen, not because you just love capturing the queen, but because you can tell that you're more likely to win if you've captured your opponent's queen than if you haven't. So, capturing the queen as an instrumental goal towards the goal of winning the game. So how does this work with money? Well, let's imagine that there's a total stranger, and you don't know what he wants out of life. You don't know what his goals are. Maybe he wants to win a marathon. Maybe he wants to kill cancer. Maybe he just wants a really nice stamp collection.
cues.zh: 比如在国际象棋里，你想吃掉对手的后，并不是因为你单纯喜欢吃后，而是因为你清楚，吃了对方的后赢面会大得多。所以，吃后只是为了赢得比赛而采取的工具性目标。那这跟钱有什么关系呢？设想有个完全陌生的人，你不知道他的人生追求是什么，也不知道他的目标是什么。也许他想跑赢马拉松，也许他想攻克癌症，也许他只是想拥有一套很棒的邮票收藏。

cues.en: But I can predict that if I were to go over to him and offer him a big stack of money, he'd be happy to take it. How can I predict this person's actions, even though I don't know his goals? Well, a guy who wants to win a marathon, if I give him money he could buy some nice running shoes, or he could hire a personal trainer or something like that. A guy who wants to cure cancer could give that money to a cancer charity, or maybe use it to help him to go to university and study science to cure cancer himself. And a guy who wants to collect stamps could... buy some stamps.
cues.zh: 但我敢预言，如果我走过去给他一大叠钱，他肯定会欣然接受。既然我都不知道他的目标，又怎么能预测他的行为呢？你看，想跑赢马拉松的人，有了钱就能买双好跑鞋，或者请个私人教练之类的。想攻克癌症的人，可以把钱捐给癌症慈善机构，或者用这笔钱供自己上大学去钻研科学，亲自去攻克癌症。至于想集邮的人嘛……可以拿去买邮票。

cues.en: So the point is, even though none of these people value money as a terminal goal, none of them want money just for the sake of having money. Nonetheless, they all value money as an instrumental goal. The money is a way to get them closer to their goals. And even though they all have different terminal goals, this goal of getting money happens to be instrumentally valuable for all of their different goals. That makes getting money a convergent instrumental goal. It's a goal that's an instrumental goal for a wide variety of different terminal goals.
cues.zh: 所以关键在于，即便这些人都不把金钱当成终极目标，没人单纯为了拥有金钱而想要金钱。但尽管如此，他们都把金钱视为工具性目标。金钱是让他们更接近目标的一种途径。而且即便他们都有不同的终极目标，赚钱这个目标碰巧对他们所有的不同目标都具有工具价值。这就让赚钱成了一个趋同性工具目标。它是一个能为各种不同终极目标服务的工具性目标。

cues.en: So, since money is a convergent instrumental goal, if you make the assumption that everybody values money, it turns out to be a fairly good assumption. Because whatever you value, money is going to help you with that. And that makes this assumption useful for making predictions, because it allows you to predict people's behaviour to some extent, without knowing their goals. So, what other convergent instrumental goals are there? Well, an obvious one is self-preservation.
cues.zh: 所以，既然金钱是一个趋同性工具目标，如果你假设人人都看重金钱，这个假设其实相当靠谱。因为无论你重视什么，金钱都能帮得上忙。这使得该假设在做预测时非常有用，因为它能让你在不知道人们目标的情况下，在一定程度上预测他们的行为。那么，还有哪些趋同性工具目标呢？显然，自我保护就是其中之一。

cues.en: Most agents, with most goals, will try to prevent themselves from being destroyed. Now, something like a thermostat or a chess AI, they're not self-aware. They don't understand that they can be destroyed, and so they won't take any actions to avoid it. But if an agent is sophisticated enough to understand that being destroyed is a possibility, then avoiding destruction is a convergent instrumental goal. Humans, of course, generally act to avoid being killed, but humans, as evolved agents, implement this in a way that might obscure the nature of the thing.
cues.zh: 大多数智能体在追求大多数目标时，都会竭力避免被摧毁。当然，像温控器或国际象棋 AI 这类东西，它们并没有自我意识。它们意识不到自己会被摧毁，所以也不会采取任何行动来避免这一点。但如果一个智能体足够复杂，能理解被摧毁是一种可能，那么避免被摧毁就会成为一个收敛性工具目标。人类当然通常也会努力避免被杀害，但作为进化而来的智能体，人类实现这一目标的方式可能会掩盖这件事情的本质。

cues.en: The point is that self-preservation need not be a terminal goal. An agent need not necessarily value self-preservation just for the sake of continuing to exist for its own sake. For example, suppose you had a software agent, an AGI, which had a single terminal goal of making as many paperclips as possible. It would try to prevent you from turning it off, not because it wants to live, but simply because it can predict that future worlds in which it's turned off
cues.zh: 关键在于，自我保全并不一定非得是最终目标。智能体不一定非要为了“继续存在”本身而重视自我保全。举个例子，假设你有一个软件智能体，也就是一个 AGI，它的唯一最终目标就是制造尽可能多的回形针。它会竭力阻止你把它关掉，这并不是因为它想活下去，而只是因为它能预见到：一旦自己被关掉，未来的世界

cues.en: will contain far fewer paperclips, and it wants to maximise the number of paperclips. But suppose you said to it, I've thought of a better way to implement your software that will be more effective at making paperclips, so I'm going to turn you off and wipe all of your memory, and then create a new version that's better at making paperclips. This is pretty clearly the destruction of that first agent, right? You're wiping all of its memories and creating a new system that works differently, that thinks differently. But the paperclip agent would be fine with this, because it can see that
cues.zh: 所包含的回形针就会少得多，而它想要把回形针的数量最大化。但假设你对它说：我想到了一种能更好地实现你软件的方法，造回形针会更高效，所以我打算先关掉你，抹掉你的全部内存，然后再创建一个更擅长造回形针的新版本。很显然，这对于第一个智能体来说就是彻底毁灭，对吧？你抹掉了它的所有记忆，创造了一个运行方式不同、思考方式也不同的新系统。但这个造回形针的智能体完全能接受，因为它能看出

cues.en: When you turn on its replacement, that will end up resulting in more paperclips overall. So it's not really about self-preservation itself, it's just that, practically speaking, most of the time, you can't achieve your goals if you're dead. On the other hand, suppose we were going to turn off the agent and change its goal. We were going to change it so that it doesn't like paperclips anymore, it actually wants to collect stamps. Here, you're not really destroying the agent, just modifying it.
cues.zh: 当你启动它的替代者时，最终结果会产生更多的回形针。所以这其实无关自我保全本身，只是在实际中，绝大多数情况下，要是你死了，就无法达成目标了。另一方面，假设我们要关掉这个智能体并改变它的目标。我们要把它改成不再喜欢回形针，而是想去集邮。在这里，你并没有真正摧毁这个智能体，只是修改了它。

cues.en: But you've got a problem again, because the agent can reliably predict that if this modification happens and it becomes a stamp collector, the future will contain not nearly as many paper clips, and that's the only thing it cares about right now. So we've got another convergent instrumental goal, goal preservation. Most agents with most goals, again, if they're sophisticated enough to realize that it's a possibility, will try to protect their goals from being modified.
cues.zh: 但问题又来了，因为智能体完全可以预见到，一旦这种修改发生，它变成了集邮者，未来的回形针数量就会大大减少，而这恰恰是它目前唯一在乎的事情。于是我们又得到了另一个趋同性工具目标：目标保全。对于大多数拥有各种目标的智能体，只要它们足够聪明、能意识到存在这种可能性，就会竭力保护自己的目标不被篡改。

cues.en: because if you get new goals, you'll stop pursuing your current goals, so you're unlikely to achieve your current goals. Now, for humans, this doesn't come up much because modifying a human's goals is fairly difficult. But still, if you suppose we were to go to the guy who wants to cure cancer and offer him some magic pill that's going to change his brain so that he doesn't care about cancer anymore and he actually wants to collect stamps, if we say, look, this is actually really good because cancer is really hard to cure. It's actually a large collection of different diseases, all of which need different approaches, so you're very unlikely
cues.zh: 因为一旦你有了新目标，就会放弃现有的目标，那你大概率就无法实现目前的目标了。当然，对人类来说这并不常见，因为要改变一个人的目标相当困难。但退一步讲，假设我们去找一个一心想治愈癌症的人，给他一颗神奇药丸，吃了就能改变大脑，让他不再关心癌症，反而只想去集邮；如果我们跟他说：“瞧，这其实超划算，因为癌症极难攻克，它本质上包含一大堆不同的疾病，每种都需要不同的应对方案，所以你几乎不可能

cues.en: to discover a cure for all of them. But on the other hand, stamp collecting is great. You can just go out and buy some stamps and you can put them in a book and look at them. I don't really know what stamp collectors do, is that? Anyway, is this guy who wants to cure cancer going to take that pill? No, he's going to say hell no, I'm not taking your crazy stamp pill. Even though this isn't a terminal goal for him, he doesn't value valuing curing cancer, right? He doesn't have a goal of having a goal of curing cancer.
cues.zh: 找到治愈所有癌症的方法。但集邮就不一样了，集邮多棒啊，你随时能去买几张邮票，夹进集邮册里欣赏——我其实不太清楚集邮的人都干嘛，大概就这样吧？”不管怎样，那个想攻克癌症的人会吃这颗药丸吗？肯定不会，他会说：“开什么玩笑，我才不吃你这疯癫的集邮药丸。”尽管这对他而言并非终极目标，他珍视的并不是“珍视治愈癌症”这件事本身，对吧？他并没有一个“把攻克癌症当作目标”的目标。

cues.en: It's just that he believes that if he gave up curing cancer to become a stamp collector, that would result in a lower chance of cancer being cured. So preserving your terminal goals is instrumentally useful, whatever those goals are. Another convergent instrumental goal is self-improvement. Notice that the guy who wants to cure cancer, part of his plan is to go to university and study science so that he can learn how to research cancer cures. And the guy who wants to run a marathon, part of his plan is he wants to train and improve his physical performance.
cues.zh: 只是他认为，如果放弃攻克癌症去集邮，治愈癌症的希望就会变得更渺茫。因此，无论你的最终目标是什么，保持这些目标都是一种有用的工具性手段。另一个趋同工具性目标是自我提升。大家注意，那个想攻克癌症的人，他计划的一部分是去上大学读理科，这样才能学会如何研发癌症疗法。而那个想跑马拉松的人，他的部分计划则是去训练并提升体能。

cues.en: Both of these things are improving yourself, and something like this comes up quite often in human plans. Again, this isn't a terminal goal. The guy who wants to cure cancer doesn't want to get a degree just because he wants a degree. He wants to become a person who's more effective at curing cancer. Now, there's another way of improving yourself, which is not really available to human beings, but is available to AI systems, which is directly modifying your mind to improve your own intelligence. You're not just adding information to your mind, you're actually making it more powerful.
cues.zh: 这两件事都是在自我提升，而类似的做法在人类的规划中非常普遍。这同样不是最终目标。想攻克癌症的人并不是为了拿学位而拿学位。他是想成为一个能更有效攻克癌症的人。不过，还有另一种自我提升的方式，人类其实做不到，但 AI 系统却可以，那就是直接修改自己的大脑来提升智力。你不仅是在往脑子里补充信息，而是在切实增强它的能力。

cues.en: For example, you might be able to rewrite your code so that it works better or runs faster. Or you might be able to just acquire more computing power. The more computing power you have, the deeper and faster you're able to think, the better you are at making plans, and therefore the better you are at achieving your goal, whatever that goal is. So computing power is kind of like money. It's a resource which is just very broadly useful, which means we can expect acquiring that resource to be a convergent instrumental goal. And speaking in the broadest possible terms,
cues.zh: 比如，你可以重写自己的代码，让它表现更好、运行更快，或者直接获取更多的算力；拥有越多的算力，你思考得就越深、越快，制定计划的能力就越强，因而也就越能达成你的目标，无论那个目标是什么；所以算力有点像金钱，是一种用途极为广泛的资源，这意味着获取这种资源往往会成为一种收敛性工具目标；而从最广泛的意义上来说，

cues.en: Almost all plans need resources in the form of matter and energy. If you want to build something, whether that's stamps or paperclips or computing hardware or robots or whatever, you need matter to build it out of, and energy to build it with, and probably energy to run it as well. So we can expect agents with a wide range of goals to try to acquire a lot of resources.
cues.zh: 几乎所有的计划都需要物质和能量形式的资源；如果你想制造某些东西，不管是邮票、回形针、计算硬件还是机器人等等，你都需要物质来制造它，需要能量来进行生产，可能还需要能量来维持它的运转；因此我们可以预见，拥有各种不同目标的智能体都会试图去攫取大量的资源。

cues.en: So, without really assuming anything about an AGI, other than that it will have goals and act to achieve those goals, we can see that it's likely that it would try to prevent itself from being shut down, try to prevent itself from being modified in important ways that we want to modify it, try to improve itself and its intelligence to become more powerful, and try to acquire a lot of resources.
cues.zh: 所以，即便我们不对AGI做任何预设，只假设它拥有目标并会采取行动来实现这些目标，我们也能看出：它很可能会极力防止自己被关机，阻止我们以重要的方式去修改它，努力提升自身及其智能以变得更强大，并试图获取大量的资源。

cues.en: This is the case for almost all terminal goals, so we can expect any generally intelligent software agents that we create to display this kind of behaviour, unless we can specifically design them not to. I want to end the video by saying thank you to all of my excellent Patreon supporters. It's these people. And in this video I'm especially thanking James McEwan, who looks a lot like the Stanford buddy, and has been a patron for nine months now. Thank you so much.
cues.zh: 几乎所有的终极目标都会导致这种情况，因此我们可以预见，只要我们创造出通用智能软件智能体，它们就会表现出这种行为，除非我们专门针对这点进行设计以防发生。视频的最后，我想感谢所有在Patreon上支持我的优秀赞助者们。就是这些人。本期视频我还要特别感谢James McEwan，他长得很像斯坦福的那个小伙伴，而且已经赞助我九个月了。非常感谢大家。

cues.en: for all of your support. And thank you all for watching. I'll see you next time.
cues.zh: 感谢大家的大力支持。也谢谢大家的观看。我们下次再见。
